h1: How Play-Based Learning Can Transform Education in India

props.title: How Play-Based Learning Can Transform Education in India
props.summaryText: Play-based learning is now part of Indian education policy. What it means in practice, why it works, and how schools can bring it into classrooms and playgrounds.
props.author: meera-iyer
props.imageAlt: Teacher and student in a classroom

takeaways.text: Play-based learning uses guided and free play to teach concepts and skills.
NEP 2020 emphasises play- and activity-based learning in the foundational stage (ages 3 to 8).
It builds understanding, language, social skills and motivation, not only fun.
Outdoor spaces and play equipment can support it as much as classroom materials.

faq.a: Play-based learning is an approach in which children learn concepts and skills through play, both free play they lead and guided play that a teacher shapes towards a learning goal, using materials, games, stories and the outdoor environment.

faq.q: Is play-based learning part of NEP 2020?
faq.a: Yes. NEP 2020 emphasises flexible, multi-faceted, play-based and activity-based learning, especially in the foundational stage for children aged 3 to 8.

faq.q: How can schools start with play-based learning?
faq.a: Train teachers, set aside time for guided play, use hands-on materials, take lessons outdoors, and design play spaces with elements for counting, building, role play and exploration.
